messages:
maria_support: Customer (Acme) reporting intermittent 502/504s on Hosted API streaming since yesterday afternoon. They say it spikes when they send a ~1.2MB initial payload + streaming followups. They gave a curl repro and a few request IDs. Can we triage?

anya_cust_success: looped in — customer is on paid plan and wants an ETA. they see ~20% failure rate on streaming sessions. non-streaming requests OK. :frowning:

jasper_oncall: on it. any request ids or traces? envoy/request ids would help. also which region?

maria_support: sent repro via DM (curl below) and request ids: rId=acme-98765, acme-98786, acme-98790. region: us-west2. curl:```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant: acme" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @big_payload.json https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream
```

sam_eng_sre: quick look at ingress logs for those rIds: seeing Envoy upstream resets and 502 responses. snippet:```
[2026-03-16T14:05:12.123Z] rId=acme-98765 upstream reset before response: stream error: stream reset (reason: REFUSED_STREAM)
[2026-03-16T14:05:12.124Z] rId=acme-98765 response_code=502 envoy_cluster=auth-backend
```

sam_eng_sre: also seeing h2 GOAWAY from auth-backend around same time, followed by a burst of new connections. suspect connection reuse + short-lived token rotation race. not 100% yet.

jasper_oncall: interesting that non-streaming path fine. streaming keeps the h2 stream open for long time; if backend resets the connection during token refresh it can break the stream and cause 502/504 to front-end. any recent deploys to auth or edge?

maria_support: there was an auth service deploy 90m before the first customer report. ops says it touched the token cache invalidation logic.

sam_eng_sre: reproduce attempt: used the provided big_payload + open streaming connection and hammered parallel streams. saw the same failure pattern when token refresh happened on auth-backend and we had pooled h2 connections reused. repro steps (short):```
1) POST large initial payload to /v1/stream with X-Tenant header
2) keep connection open and send followup frames every 2s for ~30s
3) trigger token rotation on auth-backend (dev-only endpoint)
4) ~10-20% of streams fail with upstream reset -> 502
```

maria_support: customer cannot trigger token rotation themselves; but they can flip to non-streaming as a workaround. they asked for a less disruptive fix.

jasper_oncall: mitigation options: 1) short term: route this customer's traffic to a fresh connection pool (no reuse) or to a different auth cluster copy; 2) disable streaming on tenant (workaround); 3) longer: make edge resilient to auth-backend transient GOAWAY during token rotation (avoid returning 502 when auth backend resets mid-stream).

sam_eng_sre: pushed a quick route change for acme in us-west2 to use a non-reused cluster host (drain + new pool). deployed at 14:27 UTC. monitoring now.

deploy-bot: rollout: promoted route-change:acme-noreuse -> us-west2 (id: rc-20260316-01) :white_check_mark:

maria_support: told customer we rolled a temporary route change and to test. they just confirmed lower error rate in the last 10m (from ~20% -> ~1%). :relieved:

anya_cust_success: customer happy for now but wants permanent fix and postmortem. please coordinate with eng-ml and infra.

sam_eng_sre: next steps: 1) reproduce in staging and add regression test for streaming + token rotation; 2) add a retry/fallback path in edge so a mid-stream upstream connection reset tries a transparent failover to another host instead of immediately returning 502 for the whole stream; 3) roll back the problematic auth cache invalidation change if needed.

jasper_oncall: filing an incident ticket and tagging eng-runtime + auth team. incident id: I-2026-0316-9. I'll own the postmortem.

maria_support: thanks. closing customer escalation for now (they're on monitor). will update thread when postmortem ready. :thumbsup:
